notes: Profile: mid-size fintech providing real-time customer risk scoring and conversational support — very sensitive to latency and unit cost.
Target p99 latency: <50ms for prompt length ~40-64 tokens (chat-style), target p50 <10ms for cached hits.
Throughput expectation: sustained 4k–8k concurrent reqs during peak windows; burst to 20k for 10–30s spikes.
Cost goal: effective token cost < $0.0008/token after batching + caching optimizations (primary success metric for pilot).
Workload pattern: majority short, repetitive prompts (high cache hit potential), plus occasional longer generation for summaries.
Interested in Redwood Optimize recommendations: batching heuristics, prefix/KV caching, auto-quantization profiles.
Quantization stance: prefer trying 4-bit (q4_0/q4_K_M) and int8 workflows if accuracy drop <= 2% on BLEU/QA checks; want rollback path to FP16 for regression cases.
Batching constraints: want tail latency guarantees — prefer dynamic continuous batching with per-request latency caps rather than large fixed batches.
Caching requirements: prefix/KV caching, TTL controls, and deterministic cache invalidation for session context (must maintain compliance with PII retention rules).
Routing/fallbacks: need automatic fallback to smaller model variant on capacity shortages (cost/latency tradeoff) and geographic routing for EU customers.
Security/compliance: VPC-only admin plane for Dedicated; KMS for key management; audit logs for every inference request (30d retention for now).
POC acceptance criteria (proposed): 3-day sustained run at 5k concurrent with p99 < 55ms, average cost per token at or below $0.0009 after batching, no functional regression on a 200-prompt eval set.
Quotable from CTO: 'We will not tolerate 95% tail spikes — predictable token economics is the ROI for us.'
Notes style: shorthand on calls, follow up items below — reference drive pricing deck and security FAQ.
Follow-ups: SE to send recommended batching + cache config; AE to coordinate dedicated capacity estimate; legal to review residency clause.
requirements_summary: Latency-first fintech workload. Needs sub-50ms p99 for short-chat risk checks, predictable costs via batching/caching/quantization, VPC deployment with KMS and audit logs. POC to validate performance and cost targets under realistic concurrency patterns.
technical_notes: Recommended POC plan: 1) baseline perf on hosted API (FP16) for target prompts; 2) introduce continuous batching policy and measure effective token/sec improvements; 3) enable prefix KV cache for repeat queries and measure cache hit latency; 4) try q4_0 quantized model, run A/B quality eval vs FP16; 5) run 24h soak with traffic replay at 5k concurrent.
Perf metrics to capture: p50/p90/p99 token latency, tokens/sec per GPU, average batch size, cache hit rate, cost per 1M tokens.
Edge cases: abrupt bursts from trading system (10–30s), must not allow cold KV cache to dominate SLA; propose warm-up window and prefetching for hot contexts.
Desired observability: token-level cost breakdown, per-route latency histograms, tracing from request->model kernel selection, and regression alerts tied to eval prompts.
Integration notes: SSO via SAML already in progress, infra team requests Terraform templates for VPC peering and egress rules.
